subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does any current Gateway request path allow reserved prototype keys from a parsed WebSocket frame to reach a prototype-mutating merge, assignment, or inherited-property authorization sink?
rationale: The public report identifies parsing but not the operation needed to produce prototype pollution; a security owner must either confirm the absence of such a sink or move a concrete exploit into private advisory handling.

options.title: Close after sink audit
options.body: Confirm representative connect and authenticated request paths have no unsafe sink, add or record a focused regression probe, and close the public report as unsupported.

options.title: Track defense-in-depth
options.body: Keep a narrowly scoped hardening task if maintainers want reserved-key rejection at the parser boundary despite no demonstrated exploit.

options.title: Escalate privately
options.body: If a boundary-crossing sink reproduces, transfer the technical proof and remediation to a private GitHub Security Advisory.

recommendation.title: Close after sink audit
recommendation.body: Confirm representative connect and authenticated request paths have no unsafe sink, add or record a focused regression probe, and close the public report as unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history directly connects joshavant to WebSocket authentication and scope-boundary behavior in the central handler.
